profile.headline: Software Engineer at Raytheon Technologies
profile.summary:
Graduated in B.S. in Computer Science  with experience in gathering requirements, developing, and delivering software solution.
Previously an Undergraduate Researcher at California State University, Fullerton for emotional recognition software, under natural language processing domain, and a software developer sponsored by Unisys Corp. and employed by California State  University, Fullerton.

positions.title: Software Developer/ Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
I collaborated in a  team which consisted of 3 grad students and 3 undergrads, and we were tasked to enhance one of the companies software tools.  The development was executed using Agile software development life cycle where we used Jira, a SCRUM tool, to guide and monitor our progress. I participated in weekly meetings with the engineers to discuss progress, new challenges, and reviews of the current development. 

From this experience, I have gathered requirements, devised new solutions, implemented features, tested code implementation, integrated code into a large codebase, documented the code and product, and delivered a software product to be used in a corporation's business operations with a collaborative team.

The development of the visual studio extension tool was a great success and was delivered on time at the end of our contract.

The project was sponsored by Unisys Corp.

positions.title: Instructional Student Assistant
positions.description:
As an Instructional Student Assistant, my responsibilities are to:
- Grade homework
- Give critical feedback to help students understand Data Structure concepts
- Determine grading rubric with professors and other (ISA) graders
- Attend meetings
- Perform detailed inspection in the case of academic dishonesty

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
I belonged to a team of undergraduate students with a goal to utilize machine learning to predict human emotions using utterances. Audio file recordings are used to extract predictor variables. The extracted data are used to train the machine learning model that, in theory, predicts emotion using only audio stream.

Our research has been accepted and presented at the 8th IEEE Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC) 2018 held in Las Vegas. 

The link to the publication can be found in my publications section below.

positions.title: Web Dev. Project Manager
positions.description:
Hosted workshop to educate club members regarding the use of git, HTML, and CSS basics.
Participated in Creative Coding to teach girl scouts simple computer science and engineering activities. Such activities are coding in Minecraft to explain basic control structures, building a basic circuit in a breadboard to light an LED to demonstrate how current flows and introduced them to many other sciences and engineering task.

positions.title: Teacher and Technical Specialist
positions.description:
Taught 4th - 6th grade students how to create  platform games using Stencyl software. Taught the fundamentals of circuitry using, kids friendly, LittleBits. LittleBits is a quick snap-on circuits that simulate the use of breadboard with input and output functionalities.
Acted as the main technician during the position to troubleshoot computers, projectors, audio, and visual output.

positions.title: Honors Society Club
positions.description: As the Webmaster officer, I developed the club website using HTML and CSS with open sourced JavaScript. I maintained and scaled the website constantly during my time as an officer. Alpha Gamma Sigma is an honors club which contributed to the Los Angeles County community by participating as volunteers for Non-profit organizations.

honors.title: Dean's List Fall 2015
honors.issuer: Issued by College of Engineering and Computer Science Cal State Fullerton
